feature: Claude Code CLI subscription usage caps classify as a quota, not a transport fault
why: Reported live 2026-09-19: a spent 5h Fable bucket on claude-bpx-12 announced 'Model fallback (connection issue)'. Any relay driving the genuine claude binary (claude-bpx-N, claude-cpx, claude-cpr) surfaces a cap as the CLI's own sentence "You've hit your session limit - resets 2:20pm (UTC)"; when the SDK THROWS that instead of yielding a result frame, the relay wraps it in a 5xx, so status-code classification returned server_error and the announce fell to the generic 'connection issue' floor. Three coupled behaviours: (1) classify_api_error matches the cap sentence BEFORE status-code classification (same position as account_blocked, for the same two-surface reason) and returns rate_limit; (2) extract_api_error_context derives the quota WINDOW and reset from the sentence, because these relays send no anthropic-ratelimit-unified-* headers - a named-UTC clock resolves to an epoch, an unzoned one is deliberately NOT guessed and falls back to literal text; (3) the announce rider reads '<model> usage exhausted' rather than 'rate limit', which describes a request-rate throttle. Scoped on purpose: only a BOUND quota window earns the exhaustion wording. A parity merge resolving error_classifier.py toward upstream silently restores the original symptom with no import error and no red test outside the canary file. RED-PROVEN 5/5 against merge-shaped mutations (2026-09-19): (a) agent/error_classifier.py ~L1262 disable the `if _CLAUDE_CLI_USAGE_CAP_RE.search(error_msg):` branch -> 4 fail; (b) ~L398 narrow _CLAUDE_CLI_USAGE_CAP_RE to a bare 'hit your usage limit' substring -> 4 fail; (c) agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py ~L5194 disable the sentence-derived `if "quota_window" not in context:` block -> 2 fail; (d) agent/chat_completion_helpers.py ~L2960 revert `_reason_label = f"{_who} usage exhausted"` to the flat label -> 1 fail; (e) ~L2750 drop the `quota_window_reset_text` fallback -> 1 fail. Relay-side half: Kyzcreig/claude-bpx#174 (test bridge/test/unit-sdk-thrown-error-result-classification.test.js). THE TWO HALVES ARE NOT REDUNDANT - measured 2026-09-19 by neutralizing each in turn: both present gives 'claude-fable-5-1 usage exhausted - 5h limit, resets in 11h'; harness half gone degrades to a bare 'rate limit' (relay tests still pass); relay half gone still gives 'usage exhausted - 5h limit'. A green relay suite therefore does NOT prove the user-visible label survived. test_relay_429_alone_does_not_carry_the_window pins that asymmetry (RED-proven: disable the sentence-derived quota-window block in agent_runtime_helpers.py ~L5194).

feature: whatsapp opt-in gate: a display/behaviour key in whatsapp: never auto-enables the adapter; a dead writer's platforms entries are dropped on every status write (t_83ff59d4)
why: Measured 2026-10-18: 7 gateways (aegis, argus, athena, cadmus, daedalus, daedalus-opus, momus) booted DEGRADED with whatsapp: fatal whatsapp_not_paired since >=2026-09-26 although none ever had WhatsApp. Their config carried only whatsapp: {gateway_restart_notification: false}. config_env._plugin_is_configured probes is_connected with a transient enabled=True, and whatsapp's _is_connected returned True for 'enabled and any extra', so the probe defeated the #31116 gate. _is_connected now means opt-in: WHATSAPP_ENABLED truthy; an explicit YAML enabled: true is already enabled and never probed; a leftover paired creds.json is not an opt-in (removing WHATSAPP_ENABLED is the documented disable, Prism #2069 r1). Swept every registered plugin's is_connected with the same transient view + behaviour keys: only whatsapp hit. Second half: the startup status write reloaded gateway_state.json and kept bare-key platform entries from the previous pid, so whatsapp: fatal outlived the disable; write_runtime_status(drop_stale_platforms=True) at startup drops entries whose writer (writer_pid + writer_start_time) is no longer running; a live writer keeps its entries (Prism #2069 r1). Parity-merge risk: upstream's whatsapp _is_connected carries the same 'enabled and extra' shape; a merge taking it brings the DEGRADED boot back with every upstream test green.

feature: fallback banner: one cause record per failover, a timer never becomes the cause; relay seat/route/quota window carried onto every failover row (t_94a2b0e4)
why: Measured 2026-10-18 over 14 days of blackbox fallback_events (242 failovers): 138 banners carried a claim the evidence contradicts. Live 15:55:21 PT banner 'pool sub stalled mid-turn ... no first byte in 614 s on claude-alr (seat unknown — cut before headers)': sub-vps-10 had answered 429 five_hour rejected at 15:45:20, the harness slept the 600 s Retry-After, and the wall budget then cut the retry; stash_api_error kept only the LATEST failing call, so the timer overwrote the 429, its seat, route id and class. agent/fallback_cause.py captures a FailoverCause at the first error of the attempt block (cleared by a served call, a failover row or a turn start), counts retry sleeps against it (turn_api_error note_wait), and build_row classifies and renders a timer-ended block from it ('Fable 5h limit (Anthropic 429) on sub-vps-10; retried after a 600 s wait, moved on at 614 s'); the announce label comes from the same row. The last relay attribution (x-relay-seat / x-pool-served-by, x-pool-route-id, x-relay-quota-window or Anthropic unified claim) rides every failover row; an absent seat reads 'relay sent no seat' / 'relay sent no headers', never a bare unknown. The wall-budget notice reads the same record: while the lane sleeps a Retry-After after a 429/503 it posts '⏳ waiting 150 s: Fable 5h limit on sub-vps-10 (Anthropic 429), retrying then falling back' (notice_due is not polled during a sleep, so turn_api_error posts a due notice before sleeping), never 'turn in progress (buffering lane)' with nothing in flight (Ace 2026-10-18 21:16, 21:12 fixture). A budget cut with no prior error on a buffering pool lane reads 'no reply in N s', head 'no reply within the turn budget'. Label/detail: pool_pressure and headless bridge codes take their label from the rider's cause; an xai spending-limit 403 reads 'out of credits', not 'OAuth revoked (401)'. Spec plans/2026-10-18_fallback-announce-truth-SPEC.md F1/F2 (F3 relay classification and F4 truth audit are separate cards). Parity-merge risk: turn_api_error.py and chat_completion_helpers.py are upstream files; resolving them toward upstream drops note_wait / clear / the reason override silently.

why: Ace 2026-10-22 13:43/14:06 PT (#github-alternatives, ruling option b): a goal armed with --checkin-minutes 30 got '[Continuing toward your standing goal]' every 2-6 min on a busy board (session 20261018_220948_05ec4d95, 12:12..13:48) because every kanban wake / review-deadman page / NO_REPLY answer was followed by a continuation turn that re-read unchanged state. Not a spacing timer: the continuation edge is gated on the turn's tool-call effect class; judge done/blocked/wait/budget verdicts still run every turn. Kill switch goals.nudge_on_read_only_turns: true.

feature: turn-lease flush window: an inbound while the previous turn still holds the turn lease (slot released, persist/deliver running) is queued, not dispatched; stale holder = invalidated, not superseded; a lease rejection holds the prompts queued behind it (t_d659b247)
why: 2026-10-24 14:45 Apollo default gateway: _run_agent released the turn slot at 'response ready' while _handle_message held the turn lease through a ~170 s persist+deliver; a same-key kanban wake was dispatched as a fresh turn (gen 3), the registry read the live gen-2 holder as 'stopped and draining' because gen 2 was no longer current, clipped the wait to 5 s and bounced it, and Ace's voice message queued behind gen 3 was dropped with the bounce. Fixed by: _hm_queue_during_lease_flush (queue while a lease token is still held), PersistentState.invalidated_run_generation + is_generation_invalidated (supersession is not invalidation), _hm_lease_rejection_reply (hold + count queued prompts on a fail-closed rejection). The lease and its stale-holder predicate are fork-only, so a parity merge resolving these files toward upstream silently reopens all three.

feature: idle-TTL-evicted AIAgent closes its per-agent LCM context-engine clone (release_clients/close -> _shutdown_context_engine)
why: 2026-10-23 Apollo gateway EMFILE wedge: 4,200 fds against a 4,096 soft limit, ~1,996 of them lcm.db handles leaked by idle-TTL-evicted agents whose per-agent LCM context-engine clone was never shut down; session storage and model-preference reads failed. Fixed by hermes-agent#2237 (squash 84975a7787e, 2026-10-24): AIAgent._shutdown_context_engine() called once from release_clients() and close(), tolerant of engines without shutdown() and of shutdown errors. tests/tools/test_delegate_child_lifecycle.py::_real_agent_methods stubs _shutdown_context_engine; keep that stub in sync. Upstream has no _shutdown_context_engine (0 hits in upstream/main run_agent.py): PR shape is a re-author patching run_agent.py release_clients()/close(); repro = build an agent with a context engine, evict it, count open engine handles.

feature: SessionDB periodic PASSIVE WAL checkpoint runs on its own connection, off SessionDB._lock
why: 2026-10-25 Apollo: 19-23 state.db writers queued for 42+ s behind _try_wal_checkpoint running inside the shared SessionDB._lock write lock on a 6.25 GB state.db. Fixed by hermes-agent#2311 (merge e12b459f94df, 2026-10-26): the interval checkpoint uses a dedicated _ckpt_conn under single-flight _ckpt_lock (lock order _ckpt_lock -> _lock), the interval writer never waits on it, and close() closes the checkpoint connection. Upstream has no _ckpt_conn (0 hits in upstream/main hermes_state.py): PR shape is a re-author patching hermes_state.py _try_wal_checkpoint; repro = block a checkpoint and assert a concurrent write completes.
